question: Can the current V8 macro-union provider execute each ready expert group while later disjoint group slices are still being filled, without changing reads, bytes, compute order, buffers, or exact outputs?
hypothesis: Removing the current all-reads barrier can hide at least 50 ms/V8 of the existing 234.802-ms queued upload/graph interval under the 616.347-ms read/cache/staging interval.

scope.candidate: one existing pinned macro_union_staging_ allocation partitioned into existing disjoint group ranges; worker completion publishes group readiness; main thread executes unchanged synchronous group H2D/graph in the existing group order
forbidden: asynchronous graph return or in-flight shape-buffer reuse
scope.distinction_from_p62b: P62B tested six one-row P41/P45 calibrated-plus-late-exact jobs, not the later Width1/2/8 expert-major macro-union/direct-output/direct-async path.
scope.distinction_from_x7_ping_pong: X7 added a second 256-MiB bank and stream; this candidate must use the existing single disjoint staging allocation and synchronous graph path.

gates.smoke: one exact V8 step must preserve physical/logical bytes, read-task order, logits/state hashes, group order and fallback count; queued upload/graph wall may inflate at most 5%; continue only if projected saving is at least 50 ms/V8
gates.go: both B arms exact, zero fallback/swap, unchanged bytes/order, pooled total saving at least 50 ms/V8, and queued upload/graph wall inflation at most 5%
gates.no_go: exact but pooled saving below 50 ms/V8 or device interval inflation above 5%; delete candidate source
gates.invalid: any byte/order/hash/state mismatch, fallback, swap/OOM, wrong topology/power, or worker lifetime/error-path violation
gates.abort_implementation: abort before build if safe implementation requires any forbidden mechanism

no_go_scope: A failure closes only group-readiness overlap in the current V8 macro-union/direct-async topology. It does not reopen old P62/P41/P45 overlap or close residency, reduced physical representation, or cross-stage architectural work.
